items.detail: Operation Inherent Resolve's Iraq mission concluded Wednesday under a 2024 Baghdad-Washington transition plan; roughly 2,500 remaining U.S. forces left, with Iraq assuming full responsibility for security against ISIS remnants. Iran and aligned groups cast the exit as a win. The U.S. and Iraq say they will shift to a bilateral security relationship; concerns remain about militia influence and residual ISIS threats without U.S. air and intelligence support on the ground.
items.why: Closes a major U.S. combat footprint in Iraq and reshapes regional security against ISIS and Iran-aligned forces.

items.text: Armada Acquisition Corp. II shareholders approved the Evernorth XRP-treasury merger, a step toward a planned Nasdaq listing as XRPN.
items.detail: The noon-ET special meeting cleared the business-combination vote, according to meeting attendees reported by crypto.news; an official SEC 8-K with final tallies had not posted by evening research. Proxy materials project at least about 473 million XRP at closing if the deal closes. Approval is not the same as listing or trading — remaining closing conditions and Nasdaq requirements still apply, with completion targeted for late 2026.
items.why: Advances a heavily watched crypto SPAC toward a public XRP treasury vehicle; listing and closing are still ahead.

items.text: Tennessee halted scheduled executions after Christa Pike appeared still breathing following a lethal injection attempt.
items.detail: Witnesses said Pike still appeared to be breathing about an hour after pentobarbital was administered late Wednesday at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville; she was taken to a hospital. Gov. Bill Lee ordered a third-party review and said the remaining scheduled execution will not be carried out this year. Earlier Wednesday the Supreme Court vacated a Sixth Circuit stay (Nelsen v. Pike, 26A428), clearing Tennessee to proceed before the warrant expired at midnight; Justices Sotomayor, Kagan and Jackson dissented. Pike, 50, was convicted of the 1995 murder of Colleen Slemmer and was the only woman on Tennessee's death row.
items.why: A failed lethal injection and a statewide pause on further executions, after the Supreme Court cleared the state to proceed the same day.

items.text: The Senate confirmed Keith Sonderling as Labor secretary.
items.detail: The nomination was confirmed 47-41 on a party-line vote late Wednesday (roll call 256), with 12 senators not voting. Sonderling had been serving as acting labor secretary. The vote came after the Senate earlier Wednesday invoked cloture on the nomination 53-47.
items.why: Fills the Cabinet labor post that oversees workplace rules, wages and federal labor enforcement.

items.text: A State Department rule removed Syria from the blanket ban on U.S. defense-trade licenses.
items.detail: The International Traffic in Arms Regulations final rule, effective Oct. 1, takes Syria off ITAR §126.1's list of countries subject to a policy of denial for defense exports and imports. License requests will be reviewed case by case. The change follows the secretary's Aug. 19 defense-trade policy shift after statutory barriers, including terrorism-related restrictions, were lifted or waived. Belarus, Burma, China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea and Venezuela remain on the denial list.
items.why: Opens a path to licensed U.S. defense sales and services to Syria that were previously denied by default.

items.text: USDA rewrote Rural Energy for America grants so projects must already be built before applicants can apply.
items.detail: The Rural Business-Cooperative Service final rule, published Oct. 1 and effective Oct. 16, shifts REAP renewable-energy and efficiency grants to a post-completion model using 12 months of actual performance data. It bars solar and wind systems on Farm Service Agency–certified cropland, bars components from foreign-adversary countries, limits applicants to highest-level owners, and replaces state contests with national scoring. Comments are due Nov. 2.
items.why: Changes who can get rural energy grants and when, with new farmland and foreign-component limits.

items.text: The Yankees, Padres and White Sox each swept their MLB Wild Card Series; the Phillies forced a Game 3.
items.detail: On Wednesday the Yankees beat the Red Sox 9-2, the White Sox beat the Astros 7-3 and the Padres beat the Cubs 4-1 to advance to the Division Series. The Phillies beat the Braves 4-3 in 10 innings, forcing a decisive Game 3 on Thursday.
items.why: Three Wild Card Series are over; one winner-take-all game remains before the Division Series.

items.text: A ~50-vehicle pileup on southbound I-95 over Lake Marion closed the corridor in South Carolina for an extended period.
items.detail: The morning crash near mile marker 100 on the Orangeburg/Clarendon County line involved about 50 vehicles, including roughly 15 tractor-trailers, South Carolina Highway Patrol and local outlets said. Dense fog was reported. About 11 people were hospitalized with minor injuries; the Clarendon County coroner said there were no deaths. Northbound lanes later reopened with slow traffic; southbound lanes stayed closed while crews cleared the bridge, with an SCDOT detour at mile marker 102. Officials urged drivers to avoid the area.
items.why: A major East Coast freight and travel corridor shutdown with dozens of vehicles disabled for hours.

items.text: Cornell agreed to an independent review of its handling of a 2024 fraternity sexual-assault case as prosecutors reopen a charging look.
items.detail: After a September civil lawsuit and public backlash, Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten said his office is reexamining the case it declined to charge in 2024. On Thursday the accuser's attorney told NPR she told Cornell police in 2024 she was raped — contradicting the DA's Monday description of her statement; the DA said he had not yet obtained the full interview transcript from the university. Cornell confirmed it will bring in outside counsel for an independent probe, after Gov. Kathy Hochul called for a review. The university also edited a public FAQ that had said campus police shared all investigatory information with the DA's office.
items.why: A reopened criminal review and outside campus probe put university and prosecutor accountability under statewide scrutiny.

items.text: Yemen's Saudi-backed government announced a military campaign to retake all territory held by the Iran-backed Houthis.
items.detail: Rashad al-Alimi, head of the Presidential Leadership Council, said in a televised address Sunday that operations would continue until the country is freed from the Houthis, after de-escalation efforts were exhausted; a military spokesman told the Houthis to lay down their weapons. The Houthis seized Yemen's Red Sea coast, including the Bab al-Mandab Strait, in an offensive last month, and AFP, citing Yemeni military sources, reported they cut the road linking Taiz with Aden on Sunday. The same day, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said the group fired missiles and drones at Aramco sites in Riyadh and Khurais; Saudi Arabia had not commented.
items.why: Yemen's war is widening into an all-out fight that puts Saudi oil sites and a key Red Sea shipping lane at stake.

items.text: U.S. B-1 bombers used for Iran strikes have left Britain's RAF Fairford and returned home, the Pentagon confirmed.
items.detail: The Pentagon said Sunday that all U.S. bombers deployed to RAF Fairford had re-deployed to their home stations, without saying when they moved or why, and that the bomber force can still strike from the continental United States. The move follows a U.K. counterterrorism investigation near the base: police arrested a 25-year-old British-Iranian man in London on Thursday on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, and five U.K. nationals arrested Sept. 27 over suspicious vehicles near the base were released on bail.
items.why: The main U.S. bomber base in Europe for the Iran war is now empty amid a terrorism probe.

items.text: Russia launched 205 drones at Ukraine overnight; jet-powered drones killed one person and injured eight in Kharkiv, officials said.
items.detail: Ukraine's Air Force said the attack began at 6 p.m. Sunday Kyiv time and included 49 jet-powered Shahed-type drones; air defenses shot down or suppressed 172 by 8 a.m. Monday, with hits at 13 locations. Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov said three Banderol jet drones struck near homes in the Industrialnyi district. Separately, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Sunday the U.S. has proposed technical-level three-way talks with Russia by the end of October and that Ukraine responded positively.
items.why: Russia is following through on its vow to widen strikes as Washington pushes for new talks.

items.text: A Merit Systems Protection Board rule ending the required 12-factor review of federal workers' discipline penalties takes effect today.
items.detail: The final rule (Federal Register document 2026-18061, published Sept. 3) replaces the mandatory review of all 12 Douglas factors in misconduct appeals with a test of whether an agency's penalty is reasonable under the totality of the circumstances. It applies to appeals filed on or after Oct. 5; pending appeals stay under the old framework. Individual factors can still be raised, and material mitigating evidence must be considered.
items.why: Federal employees fighting suspensions or firings lose a checklist the board had to walk through in every case.
items.source: Federal Register / Merit Systems Protection Board

items.text: The State Department said it is monitoring a suspected fatal pneumonic plague case in Russia's Irkutsk region with the CDC.
items.detail: A State Department spokesperson told RFE/RL on Oct. 4 that the U.S. is aware of reports of a fatal suspected pneumonic plague case and is monitoring with the CDC and other agencies, and urged Russia to share accurate information quickly and openly; an HHS spokesperson confirmed the CDC is working with State. No new U.S. travel restrictions were announced, and there are no direct commercial flights between the two countries. Russia's Rospotrebnadzor says the 28-year-old Anti-Plague Institute lab technician died of pneumonia of unknown cause, found no work-linked microorganisms in testing, and calls the regional situation stable; about 200 contacts are under observation.
items.why: Washington is now formally tracking a possible plague death tied to a Russian research lab.

items.text: The Supreme Court opened its new term by turning away hundreds of appeals, including Second Amendment, COVID vaccine-mandate and "Let's Go Brandon" cases.
items.detail: Monday's order list from the justices' Sept. 28 long conference denied review in United States v. Hembree, leaving in place a 5th Circuit ruling that the federal felon-in-possession gun ban was unconstitutional as applied to a man whose prior felony was meth possession. The Court also denied two challenges to Washington state COVID-19 vaccine mandates (Petersen v. Snohomish Regional Fire and Rescue; Roberts v. Ferguson) and left in place a 6th Circuit ruling letting a Michigan school bar "Let's Go Brandon" sweatshirts. In Mullin v. National TPS Alliance, it sent the Venezuelan and Haitian Temporary Protected Status case back to the 9th Circuit in light of its June ruling in Mullin v. Doe, and it asked the Solicitor General for views in three mortgage-escrow interest cases. The Court heard its first argument of the term, Suncor Energy v. Boulder County, on whether federal law bars state climate-damage suits against oil companies.
items.why: Denials leave lower-court rulings on gun rights, vaccine mandates and student speech in force for now.
items.source: Supreme Court of the United States (order list)

items.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guards forced an inbound tanker to turn back in the Strait of Hormuz, as a third tanker in two days was hit by a projectile.
items.detail: UK Maritime Trade Operations said Monday the IRGC hailed the tanker 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, and told it to turn back or be targeted; the master complied. Separately, UKMTO said another tanker in the strait was struck by an unknown projectile that set its engine room on fire; the crew was fighting the blaze and no casualties or environmental damage were reported. Iran's parliament speaker said the strait stays closed until seven U.S. conditions are met, and President Pezeshkian called talks with Washington meaningless. Pezeshkian on Sunday accepted the resignation of Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad as exports dried up under the U.S. blockade.
items.why: Hormuz traffic and oil prices hinge on whether Iran keeps turning ships away.

items.text: The 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.31% Monday, its highest level since 2002.
items.detail: The benchmark yield rose 3.4 basis points on the day, Dow Jones Market Data reported, extending a selloff that pushed it to a 19-year high in late September. Big tech shares still lifted stocks, and the euro fell to a 17-month low against the dollar on worries about France's debt. U.S. crude for November fell 1.84% to settle at $89.43 a barrel. The 10-year yield is a benchmark for mortgage and other long-term loan rates.
items.why: Higher long-term yields push up mortgage and loan rates nationwide.

items.text: Federal price-transparency rules finalized Monday require health insurers to give cost estimates by phone and post standardized price files.
items.detail: CMS, with the Labor and Treasury departments, amended the 2020 Transparency in Coverage rules for non-grandfathered group plans and insurers. Plans must report in-network rates by provider network, drop rates for services a provider's specialty would not perform, post negotiated-rate and out-of-network files quarterly instead of monthly, lower the out-of-network reporting threshold from 20 claims to 11, add a "Price Transparency" homepage link, and have a senior official attest the data is accurate. The rules take effect 60 days after Federal Register publication; file changes apply in five months, new taxonomy, utilization and text files in 11 months, and phone cost-sharing quotes for plan years starting on or after Jan. 1, 2027. The agencies estimate about $174.5 million a year in net savings for plans from year two.
items.why: Employer and individual plan members get more usable prices before care.

items.text: The two passengers on the lost Bermuda–Boston air ambulance were named as a Bermuda mother and son; all six aboard are presumed dead.
items.detail: Bermuda police identified Marilyn Lavonne Bean, 66, and Sergio Wayne Lottimore, 41, who were aboard the Gulfstream G100 with four crew when it went missing off Nantucket around 1 a.m. Saturday. The Coast Guard suspended its search Sunday after 66 hours, and owner Latitude Air Ambulance said all aboard are presumed dead; crew names have not been released. The pilot reported electrical problems and declared an emergency as a storm approached. The NTSB said Monday the investigative jurisdiction is still being determined, working with Canada's Transportation Safety Board.
items.why: The search has ended and attention turns to why the jet went down.

items.text: A Florida school bus carrying 37 students flipped in a Winter Haven crash Monday, killing a 10th-grade girl and a Jeep occupant.
items.detail: Polk County Sheriff Grady Judd said an oncoming car crossed the center line shortly after 6 a.m. and hit the side of the bus bound for Winter Haven High School, tearing off a tire and sending the bus head-on into a Jeep that caught fire. The bus overturned onto its roof. Thirty-nine people were aboard, including the driver and the driver's daughter; five to seven people were taken to hospitals with potentially traumatic injuries, and one was in critical condition.
items.why: The sheriff called it the county's worst school-bus crash in decades.

items.text: Ukraine launched about 650 drones at Moscow overnight, killing two people in one of the largest attacks on the Russian capital in two years, Russian officials said.
items.detail: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said most of the drones were shot down, 105 of them close to the city. Moscow region Gov. Andrei Vorobyov said one person died in Radumlya and one in Barybino, and a drone set a retail warehouse on fire in Litvinovo. Reports put the injured at six to nine. The 650 figure comes from Russian officials; Ukraine has not confirmed it. Russia's Defense Ministry said it struck Ukraine's Black Sea ports of Chornomorsk and Izmail overnight.
items.why: It is a major escalation of Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russia's capital.

items.text: A tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by an unknown projectile Monday evening, starting an engine-room fire, the UK maritime agency UKMTO said.
items.detail: UKMTO cited the ship's captain and said there were no early reports of injuries. It is the third tanker struck in two days, after a crude tanker Saturday and an oil tanker and an LNG tanker Sunday. Iran's Fars news agency said Iran had acted against 13 vessels in the past seven days. Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guards turned an inbound tanker back on Monday.
items.why: Attacks on Hormuz shipping now come almost daily, keeping oil near $100 a barrel.

items.text: A Trump executive order lets off-road dyed diesel be used on highways through Dec. 31 and moves to defer the federal diesel excise tax.
items.detail: The order, "Emergency Tax Relief on Diesel Fuel," was signed Oct. 5. Treasury has five days to decide whether disaster-style relief applies; if it does, federal diesel excise tax payments are deferred for fuel used Oct. 5 through Dec. 31. The IRS must also announce within five days that it will not penalize selling or using dyed diesel on highways in that period. The White House says the deferral carries no interest or penalties and that Europe agreed to release 100 million barrels of refined diesel from its reserves over four months.
items.why: Cheaper diesel for truckers and farmers would ease freight and food costs.

items.text: Treasury warned foreign banks still doing business with Iran's financial sector that they can be sanctioned at any time, without advance notice.
items.detail: The OFAC alert, dated Oct. 5 under "Operation Economic Outcast," tells banks dealing with sanctioned Iranian banks to end those ties right away and says serving Iranian banks or their branches abroad now carries sanctions risk. OFAC also amended an Iran FAQ on restricting a foreign bank's U.S. correspondent accounts. Earlier steps include cutting Banque Misr UAE's U.S. correspondent access in August and sanctioning Turkey's Golden Global Bank and Russia's VTB Bank in September.
items.why: One Iran-linked transaction can now cost a foreign bank its access to U.S. dollars.

items.text: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces retook Dhubab and other towns near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from the Houthis, Yemeni officials said.
items.detail: The offensive, called "Yemen Dawn," also took the towns of Bab and Hadeid, according to officials and witnesses. Saudi coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said 100 fighter jets are supporting the push. A U.S. official and a regional official told AP the United States provided intelligence sharing, targeting and planning help. Government leaders say the goal is to retake Sanaa. The WHO says the fighting has killed at least 959 people.
items.why: Control of a shipping chokepoint for about 12% of world trade is shifting, with U.S. help.

items.text: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan's execution by firing squad was approved by President Trump; the U.S. military has not executed anyone since 1961.
items.detail: Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said on X that the Army secretary will set the time and place. Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist, was sentenced to death for the 2009 shooting at Fort Hood, Texas, that killed 13 people.
items.why: It would be the first U.S. military execution in about 65 years.

items.text: Kenya confirmed its first imported Ebola case, a Kenyan citizen who traveled from Congo through Uganda and died in Nairobi.
items.detail: Health Minister Aden Duale said Tuesday the patient arrived in Kenya on Saturday and was isolated and treated at Nairobi Hospital before dying.
items.why: Ebola has reached East Africa's main travel and business hub.

items.text: Televangelist Jim Bakker, whose PTL Club empire collapsed in a sex scandal and fraud conviction, has died at 86.
items.detail: His wife, Lori Bakker, said he died Monday; the cause was not immediately clear, and he had a stroke in 2020. At its mid-1980s peak, "The PTL Club" drew up to 13 million viewers a night, and the ministry ran the Heritage USA theme park in Fort Mill, S.C. He was convicted of fraud and conspiracy in 1989, sentenced to 45 years (later cut to eight) and paroled in 1994.
items.why: His downfall was one of the defining scandals of the 1980s.

items.text: Russia's overnight missile and drone attack on Ukraine killed at least 11 people, including five in a Pryluky apartment building, Ukraine's president said.
items.detail: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia fired about 70 missiles, many of them ballistic, plus attack drones at Kyiv and at least 12 regions, with energy infrastructure a key target. A missile hit a five-story apartment building in Pryluky, in the Chernihiv region, killing five and injuring 26, including five children. Two people were killed in Kyiv and two in Oleksandriia, and apartment buildings were damaged in Dnipro and Kremenchuk. The attack came on Vladimir Putin's 74th birthday. Separately, Russian officials said they intercepted almost 900 Ukrainian drones overnight.
items.why: It is one of the deadliest Russian barrages in weeks and again targets Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter.

items.text: Tropical Storm Isaias formed in the western Gulf of Mexico and is forecast to strengthen rapidly before nearing the northern Gulf Coast Friday.
items.detail: As of 4 a.m. CDT Wednesday, the National Hurricane Center put Isaias near 22.0N, 94.1W with maximum sustained winds of about 40 mph, moving east-northeast at 8 mph. Forecasters expect it to become a hurricane by Thursday. Heavy rain, gusty winds, storm surge and possible tornadoes are expected from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle. No coastal watches or warnings were in effect yet.
items.why: Gulf Coast residents from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle may face a hurricane by the weekend.

items.text: Yemen's Houthis fired ballistic missiles and drones at Aden's international airport, forcing a Cairo flight to divert, as Saudi Arabia downed a missile near Riyadh.
items.detail: Yemen's government said at least two ballistic missiles and several drones targeted the runway and terminal, with one missile landing near the runway minutes before a flight from Cairo was due; the flight was sent to Jeddah and the terminal evacuated. The Houthis said they targeted Saudi military supplies at a nearby camp. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile north of Riyadh. The Houthis also claimed attacks on Saudi airports in Riyadh and Abha. Fighting has intensified as Saudi-backed government forces push toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
items.why: The Yemen war is widening into direct attacks on civilian airports and the Saudi capital.

items.text: Anduril and the Navy will spend $6.6 billion on a new Baltimore County shipyard to build Virginia-class submarine parts, the White House announced.
items.detail: Anduril is investing $3.7 billion and the Navy committed up to $2.9 billion through a contract for the facility, called Arsenal-2, at Tradepoint Atlantic. Maryland officials said it will create more than 3,100 permanent jobs; initial operations are targeted for 2030. President Trump promoted the project Tuesday.
items.why: It is one of the largest new defense manufacturing investments aimed at the Navy's submarine backlog.

items.text: Hurricane Isaias, now packing 100 mph winds, is expected to hit the northern Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, forecasters said.
items.detail: The National Hurricane Center said Isaias could briefly reach major-hurricane strength early Friday before wind shear weakens it near landfall, most likely near the Alabama-Florida border. A life-threatening storm surge is forecast from the mouth of the Mississippi River to Suwannee, Fla., with hurricane warnings for parts of the Florida Panhandle, southern Alabama and southern Mississippi and up to 15 inches of rain in spots.
items.why: Millions on the Gulf Coast face surge, flooding and long power outages this weekend.

items.text: U.S. strikes on Iran will not resume before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, President Trump said, citing "productive discussions" with Tehran.
items.detail: Trump said on Truth Social Thursday that the naval blockade of Iran stays in full force. The post reversed his comments the night before that he was weighing pre-election strikes; Brent crude rose above $104 a barrel Thursday.
items.why: Sets the U.S. military posture in the Iran war for the next three-plus weeks.

items.text: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner meet Ukrainian officials in Miami Friday on a new joint proposal to end the war, the White House confirmed.
items.detail: A broader session with national-security advisers from the U.K., France and Germany plus NATO, the EU and U.S. European Command is set for 11:30 a.m. ET. Overnight, Russia launched 136 drones at Ukraine, killing one person in Zaporizhzhia, while Russia said it downed 505 Ukrainian drones over 19 regions.
items.why: The first major U.S.-led peace round in months, as strikes on both sides intensify.

items.text: CNN, MS NOW and Politico keep White House access through at least Tuesday after a federal judge extended his order blocking their ban.
items.detail: U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly said he will rule by Tuesday on a longer preliminary injunction. The outlets were barred from White House grounds nearly three weeks ago; their lawyer called it viewpoint discrimination.
items.why: Tests how far the White House can exclude news outlets it dislikes.

items.text: A Royal Navy intelligence sailor, Teddy Young, 24, was charged in London with preparing to pass protected information to Russia.
items.detail: Prosecutors say he kept sensitive defense and intelligence material and used the dark web to try to contact Russian authorities during his first deployment. He was remanded in custody until an Oct. 16 Old Bailey hearing; police said the case is unrelated to the RAF Fairford alert.
items.why: Another Russia espionage case inside a NATO military.

items.text: Durham, N.C., firefighter Andrew Brokes, 24, was killed in a roof collapse while searching a burning home; Gov. Josh Stein ordered flags lowered.
items.detail: Two other firefighters were hurt at the fire on Marly Drive on Oct. 8. Flags fly at half-staff across North Carolina on Oct. 9.
items.why: A line-of-duty death that has drawn statewide mourning.

items.text: The International Criminal Court itself was put under U.S. sanctions, blocking its U.S.-linked assets and barring most American dealings with it.
items.detail: Treasury's OFAC added the court to its blocked-persons list Oct. 9 under Executive Order 14203, announced alongside a State Department release. General licenses allow a wind-down through April 7, 2027, and carve out telecom and software services, pensions, and services tied to detainees.
items.why: A first-ever sanction on the whole court, not just its officials.

items.text: Fed Governor Lisa Cook will face a White House panel that will recommend whether President Trump has "cause" to fire her.
items.detail: A presidential memorandum dated Oct. 7 and published this week names economic adviser Kevin Hassett, the EEOC chair and the acting Office of Government Ethics director to investigate mortgage-statement allegations. A closed, transcribed hearing of up to four hours is set for Nov. 5 at the White House; Cook may file a follow-up statement by Nov. 10.
items.why: Sets a process for removing a sitting Fed governor after the Supreme Court's Trump v. Cook ruling.

items.text: Hurricane Isaias strengthened to a Category 3 major hurricane with 120 mph winds hours before an expected Friday-night landfall on the northern Gulf Coast.
items.detail: The National Hurricane Center's 1 p.m. CDT advisory put the center about 240 miles south of Pensacola earlier in the day, moving north-northeast at 16 mph, with tropical-storm conditions already starting on the coast. Landfall is expected this evening in the warning area, with weakening after landfall.
items.why: The season's first major U.S. hurricane landfall threat, with life-threatening surge.

items.text: The Nobel Peace Prize went to Navi Pillay, the South African jurist and former U.N. human rights chief, for promoting peace and international law.
items.detail: The Norwegian Nobel Committee cited her role in ensuring war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted. The prize, worth 12 million Swedish crowns, will be presented in Oslo on Dec. 10.
items.why: The world's best-known prize this year backs international courts.

items.text: A fully loaded crude supertanker was hit by an unknown projectile off the UAE coast, outside the Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO said.
items.detail: The strike about 13 nautical miles west of Al Jazeera, UAE, set a fire that was put out; crew status and damage were unknown. Shipping sources named the Panama-flagged GEM NO.2. It follows a tanker strike off Qatar earlier this week.
items.why: Attacks on Gulf shipping are spreading beyond Hormuz.

items.text: An ICE officer shot a man in his car with a 5-year-old in the back seat in Manhattan, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani demanded ICE halt city operations.
items.detail: The Dominican man, identified as Oscar Belgal, was wounded in the neck during an arrest Oct. 8 in Marble Hill and is held outside New York state. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said officers did not know the child was in the car and criticized the city's sanctuary policies.
items.why: A sharp new clash between New York City and federal immigration agents.

items.text: Hurricane Isaias hit the Florida Panhandle near Destin as a Category 2 storm, leaving hundreds of thousands without power in Florida and Alabama.
items.detail: The National Hurricane Center said Isaias came ashore around 9:30 p.m. ET Friday with 105 mph winds; a gauge in Panama City Beach showed water 5.6 feet above high tide. It weakened to a post-tropical cyclone early Saturday as it moved through Alabama toward the Tennessee Valley, with flooding rain expected across the Southeast this weekend. Florida, Alabama and Georgia declared states of emergency.
items.why: The first hurricane of a late-starting season struck a populated coast.

items.text: Russian diesel sanctions were waived until April 2027 after President Trump announced a deal with Putin for more than 4 million tons of fuel.
items.detail: Trump said Russia will send over 300,000 tons immediately, 500,000 in November, then more. Treasury's OFAC issued a general license allowing Russian diesel loaded on tankers as of Friday to reach the global market, weeks after Trump signed a Russia sanctions law. Ukraine's Zelenskyy called it a weak decision; Democratic senators called it a betrayal.
items.why: A sharp reversal of U.S. pressure on Russia, aimed at fuel prices before the midterms.

items.text: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck central Panama, damaging more than 400 buildings and injuring at least 27 people, with no deaths reported.
items.detail: The USGS placed the quake near Pitaloza Arriba in Herrera province at 12:56 p.m. local time Friday. Panama's civil protection agency reported damage to homes, 188 schools, 20 health facilities, bridges and roads; more than 80 aftershocks followed, one above magnitude 6.
items.why: One of the strongest quakes to hit Central America in years.

items.text: Katie Zacharia, a communications adviser at Trump's media company, was named the next White House press secretary, succeeding Karoline Leavitt.
items.detail: Trump announced the pick on Truth Social. Zacharia, an attorney and commentator who briefly worked at the Department of Homeland Security, will be his sixth chief spokesperson across two terms; Leavitt left in August. No start date was announced.
items.why: The new public face of the White House less than four weeks before the midterms.

items.text: Riyadh's main airport was hit again Saturday when a missile struck the domestic terminals complex, wounding many people, as Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia mount.
items.detail: A regional official said the missile hit the complex housing terminals 3 and 4 at King Khalid International Airport. Houthi attacks earlier in the week killed three Saudis, including a pilot, and damaged three planes. The Houthis, who did not immediately comment, accused Saudi Arabia of striking Sanaa's airport. Asked about joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis, President Trump said, "We may. We're going to look at it."
items.why: The Iran war's Yemen front is now hitting civilian air travel in the Gulf's biggest economy.

items.text: Hurricane Isaias has killed four people, two in Florida and two in Alabama, and about 670,000 customers across four states were still without power Saturday.
items.detail: In Escambia County, Fla., a woman died when a tree fell on her home and a man died of carbon monoxide from a generator running in a garage, Gov. Ron DeSantis and Sheriff Chip Simmons said; Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey confirmed two deaths. Isaias weakened to a post-tropical cyclone after landfall near Destin; forecasters warned of up to 10 inches of rain and flooding in Georgia and the Carolinas.
items.why: Deaths and outages update from this morning's landfall story.

items.text: France's police watchdog is investigating 24 cases of alleged force against students in weeks of school protests, including a 14-year-old whose jaw was broken.
items.detail: The officer who fired the tear gas canister at the 14-year-old was placed under formal investigation for assault. Authorities say 700 police officers have been injured and 6,877 people arrested, mostly minors, in more than two weeks of unrest over school conditions that Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu called the most violent in decades.
items.why: Europe's largest student unrest in years is turning into a policing fight.

items.text: An energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine was announced by President Trump, but Zelensky said the deal was "news to me" and Russian strikes continued.
items.detail: "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed," Trump posted Sunday, giving no details. Zelensky told Axios Ukraine would accept it if Putin did, but said Russian drones and airstrikes hit energy sites through the day, including Kharkiv's thermal power station No. 5. The Kremlin gave no sign it was observing a halt.
items.why: Washington is pressing Kyiv to stop its refinery strikes, the most effective weapon it has.

items.text: Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport was struck again Sunday when a projectile hit Terminal 4, and Dammam's airport was also attacked, Saudi officials said.
items.detail: The strike injured an unspecified number of people and started a fire; Saudi air defenses also intercepted a cruise missile near the Riyadh airport. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed Saturday's airport strike in a televised speech, and the Houthis named Dammam's airport, an Aramco-linked station and an Eastern Province refinery as targets. The death toll from Saturday's attack rose to 13 after an Indian national died of his injuries.
items.why: The Houthi campaign is spreading from Riyadh to Saudi Arabia's oil region.

items.text: Iran called the U.S. response to its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz "insufficient" as projectiles hit two more tankers in the strait.
items.detail: Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Washington must clarify open issues before talks can move and warned regional cables, data centers and AI facilities could become targets if fighting resumes. UKMTO reported an unidentified projectile struck an outbound tanker Sunday afternoon. Separately, U.S. Central Command said a fighter jet disabled the Panama-flagged cargo ship Ocean Molica on Saturday as it tried to run the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports.
items.why: Hormuz talks are stalled while attacks on shipping keep oil markets on edge.

items.text: The Cleveland Guardians beat the White Sox 2-0 in Game 5 to finish a comeback from 0-2 down and reach the AL Championship Series.
items.detail: Gavin Williams had 12 of Cleveland's 21 strikeouts and José Ramírez hit a two-run homer Saturday night. Cleveland is the 11th team to win a best-of-five series after losing the first two games, and the first since the 2017 Yankees. The ALCS against Tampa Bay opens Monday; the Dodgers-Brewers NLCS opens Sunday night.
items.why: A rare playoff comeback sets the final four.

items.text: India's youth protest movement vowed more demonstrations after police detained thousands, including its leaders and opposition politicians, in New Delhi on Saturday.
items.detail: Protesters demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over a voter-list revision they say favors Prime Minister Modi's BJP. Authorities sealed the Jantar Mantar protest site and suspended trains and metro service; police said Sunday all detainees were released, and protests were called for Mumbai and other cities.
items.why: A voter-roll fight is drawing the biggest youth street protests in India's capital.

items.text: Israel's former attorney general Avichai Mandelblit took the witness stand Sunday in Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial, weeks before Israel's election.
items.detail: Mandelblit indicted Netanyahu seven years ago on fraud, breach of trust and bribery charges, the first ever against a sitting Israeli prime minister. Israel votes Oct. 27.
items.why: The prosecutor who charged Netanyahu is testifying as voters decide his future.

items.court: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York
items.text: The taxpayer-funded TV ads promoting President Trump must be canceled, a federal judge in New York ordered Sunday night, including spots set to air that evening.
items.detail: U.S. District Judge Jennifer L. Rochon granted a temporary restraining order sought by Common Cause, SEIU Local 32BJ and others, finding they are likely to succeed in their claim that the roughly $20 million DHS-funded campaign misused appropriations. The order took effect at 6:45 p.m. EDT, bars the government from paying for or placing more of the ads, and lasts two weeks. The administration had told the court the campaign would end Sunday; it is the first known ruling to block the ads, which also face a DNC lawsuit.
items.why: A court has now said federal money likely cannot pay for ads praising the president weeks before the Nov. 3 midterms.
items.source: U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York (order)

items.text: Two Indian sailors are missing after a drone hit the tanker Petro Dolphin off Oman's Sohar port, as Iran's Guards warned ships running dark will be treated as hostile.
items.detail: India's Foreign Ministry said Monday the two were among 11 Indian crew aboard the Petro Dolphin when it was struck Sunday near the Sohar anchorage, outside the Strait of Hormuz; a second tanker, the Valthera, was hit by a projectile and caught fire, but its crew is safe. Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy said vessels that switch off navigation and identification systems in the strait will be dealt with as hostile, and claimed a third tanker struck a mine there Sunday.
items.why: Attacks on shipping are spreading beyond Hormuz into the Gulf of Oman.

items.text: Russia kept striking Ukraine's power sites overnight, a day after President Trump announced an energy ceasefire, and Moscow still has not said it agreed.
items.detail: Kharkiv prosecutors said Russian forces hit an energy facility on the city's outskirts Monday, after Sunday-evening strikes on power plants in Kyiv and Kharkiv caused outages; energy and rail sites in the Zhytomyr region were also hit overnight. Zelensky said Ukraine is ready to stop striking Russian energy infrastructure if Russia does the same.
items.why: The truce Trump announced is not holding on the ground.

items.text: North Korea fired several ballistic missiles toward the sea off its east coast Monday, one flying more than 900 kilometers, South Korea's military said.
items.detail: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff detected the launch from the Pyongyang area at about 9:20 a.m. local time and called it an apparent protest of the South's first hypersonic glide vehicle test last week. Japan said the missiles fell outside its exclusive economic zone. North Korea last fired a ballistic missile on Oct. 3.
items.why: Missile tests are speeding up as tensions on the peninsula rise.

items.text: The death toll from Russia's guided-bomb strike on a Zaporizhzhia apartment building rose to 23, including four children, Ukraine's emergency service said.
items.detail: Russian guided aerial bombs hit a five-story residential building in Zaporizhzhia on the morning of Oct. 10. Rescuers finished searching the site Sunday morning with 20 dead counted; the regional emergency service later raised the toll to 23, a figure President Zelensky also gave. At least 32 people were injured.
items.why: It is one of the deadliest single strikes on a Ukrainian city this year.
items.source: Ukrainska Pravda, citing Ukraine's State Emergency Service

items.text: ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News and NBC are under Justice Department investigation over whether jointly suspending White House pool coverage broke antitrust law.
items.detail: DOJ said it is examining whether the TV pool's pause in coverage of President Trump, which began Sept. 21 after the White House barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico, was an illegal group boycott under the Sherman Act. Pool coverage has since resumed, and a judge restored the barred outlets' White House access on Sept. 24. The Freedom of the Press Foundation called the probe "nonsense."
items.why: It turns a press-access fight into a federal antitrust case against the biggest TV news networks.

items.text: Tesla unveiled its long-delayed next-generation Roadster Thursday night at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, nearly nine years after first showing it.
items.detail: The reveal was livestreamed starting at 8:55 p.m. ET, two weeks after an Oct. 1 date was scrapped over weather. Tesla's Roadster page now lists three versions: a two-seat road car sold by reservation, a limited-release track version with rear SpaceX cold-gas thrusters that Tesla says reaches 0-60 mph in under 1 second, and an invite-only one-seat version Tesla says "can fly." Tesla says the thruster versions are not approved for public road use. Reuters reported that the $200,000 price from 2017 has not been updated and that reservations are still $50,000; Tesla originally promised deliveries in 2020. Musk has called the car a "small potato situation" for Tesla's finances.
items.why: It's Tesla's first new car reveal in years, though even Musk says it won't move the company's finances much.

items.text: Pope Leo XIV has lung cancer, the Vatican confirmed Tuesday, Oct. 13, after surgeons at Rome's Gemelli Hospital removed the lower lobe of his right lung.
items.detail: The Holy See Press Office said tissue examined during Tuesday's operation confirmed lung adenocarcinoma, as suspected from earlier tests. Surgeons led by Prof. Stefano Margaritora removed the lobe using a video-assisted technique; the operation lasted about 90 minutes with no complications. His schedule is cleared until at least Oct. 20. In a Thursday, Oct. 15 update, his doctors said routine checks were normal, a chest X-ray showed good recovery of the operated lung, he was carrying out daily activities independently, and his recovery is proceeding as expected. The Vatican said he resumed work from the hospital and met with a senior aide. Further tests on the removed tissue are pending.
items.why: The head of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics, 71, is being treated for cancer, with tests still pending on whether further treatment is needed.
items.source: Holy See Press Office; Vatican News

items.court: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York
items.text: The Justice Department's lawsuit against New York City's sanctuary laws was thrown out by a federal judge in Brooklyn on Thursday, leaving the city's limits on helping ICE in place.
items.detail: U.S. District Judge Ramón E. Reyes Jr. granted the city's motion to dismiss the suit the administration filed in July 2025. He found the federal government lacked standing to challenge the city's ban on police holding immigrants at federal request because state law already bars that practice, and ruled that federal law does not require local governments to share release dates or other custody information. He rejected the argument that federal law overrides the city's rules, finding the federal government cannot force local governments to assist with immigration enforcement. Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the ruling a victory for New Yorkers.
items.why: It is a court loss for the administration's campaign against sanctuary cities, and the nation's largest city keeps its rules limiting cooperation with ICE.
items.source: U.S. District Court, E.D.N.Y. (opinion via Courthouse News); Reuters

items.text: Commercial goods have stopped entering Gaza, Israel said Thursday, blaming merchants protesting Hamas fees; Palestinian importers say Israel made the decision.
items.detail: COGAT, the Israeli military body that oversees humanitarian affairs in Gaza, said no commercial goods had entered for two days after Gazan merchants suspended coordination over a 10,000-shekel (about $3,220) fee Hamas charges per truck and a demand that 30% of sales be in cash. Hamas called the fee a voluntary contribution. The head of Gaza's private truckers union said Israel imposed the halt; aid trucks and some commercial goods from Egypt still entered. COGAT said total daily truck traffic would fall by about half, to around 300.
items.why: Most of Gaza's 2 million people depend on trucked-in supplies, and commercial goods make up a large share of what enters.

items.text: The Milwaukee Brewers swept the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers to reach the World Series for the first time since 1982.
items.detail: Milwaukee won Game 4 of the National League Championship Series 6-4 Thursday night at Dodger Stadium after falling behind 4-0 on a Shohei Ohtani three-run homer. Garrett Mitchell's sixth-inning home run put the Brewers ahead and David Hamilton added a ninth-inning homer. It is the franchise's second World Series trip. Milwaukee will host Game 1 next Friday against the winner of the AL Championship Series between Cleveland and Tampa Bay.
items.why: The defending champions are out, and one of baseball's smallest markets is in the World Series.
